question.problem:
Suppose we take a random sample of size $n=96$ from a population where $36%$ of the population has a particular characteristic. Find a normal approximation for the probability that less than $28%$ of the sample has the characteristic. You may assume that the population size is significantly larger than the sample size.

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ are given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution.*

| $z$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.04\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,-1.6\,$ | $\,0.0537\,$ | $\,0.0526\,$ | $\,0.0516\,$ | $\,0.0505\,$ |
| $\,-1.5\,$ | $\,0.0655\,$ | $\,0.0643\,$ | $\,0.0630\,$ | $\,0.0618\,$ |
| $\,-1.4\,$ | $\,0.0793\,$ | $\,0.0778\,$ | $\,0.0764\,$ | $\,0.0749\,$ |
